overview: Huckleberry Mountain (6,320-6,340 ft) is a small but striking andesite peak on the Cascade Crest ridgeline between Mount Thomson and Chikamin Peak, about 5 miles northeast of Snoqualmie Pass in the Alpine Lakes Wilderness. It is not near the Middle Fork Snoqualmie/Dutch Miller Gap trail system — it's reached from the Pacific Crest Trail, which traverses its south and east slopes past Kendall Katwalk, Ridge Lake, and Alaska Mountain. The summit sits on the King/Kittitas county line. Two historic
beta: There is no true walk-up to Huckleberry's summit. The mountain's original (and for decades only) route climbs class 3-4 terrain along the ridge crest with a short, exposed low-5th-class step to top out the summit block; two later technical lines — a 5.7 South Face and a 5.6 West Face first climbed in 2001 — are more sustained rock routes. Nearly all parties, including strong scramblers, bring a rope and light rack to protect and rappel the final block.

overview: North Twin Sister (6,644 ft) is the second-highest and northernmost summit of the Twin Sisters Range, a massif of dunite (mantle-derived, olivine-rich rock) about 10 miles southwest of Mount Baker. This line follows the mountain's west ridge on solid, high-friction olivine to the north summit as an unroped scramble.
beta: Expect sustained class 3 scrambling on exceptionally solid, high-friction rock, with short class 4 steps and multiple false summits near the top.

overview: Officially "Pinnacle Peak" on USGS maps, but almost universally called The Chopping Block for its distinctive squarish, blocky summit block. It sits at the south end of the Barrier Ridge in the Southern Pickets, North Cascades National Park, dividing Terror Creek Basin from Crescent Creek Basin, and is visible from the Newhalem visitor center on clear days. beta: Climbers approach via Goodell Creek and Terror Creek to a high camp on the Stump Hollow ridge below the peak, then climb 3rd/4th class terrain with a short section of low-5th-class rock (5.4) to reach the summit. Because the Pickets guard several summits from a shared basin, parties frequently combine this peak with Mount Degenhardt, Mount Terror, or Inspiration Peak on the same trip.

overview: Ragged Edge climbs the right side of Vesper's clean north face via shallow corners, flakes and slabs, established by Darin Berdinka and Gene Pires on August 18, 2013. It's the most popular moderate line on the wall — low-angle, well-featured 5.7 climbing on ~700 ft of granite, capped by an exposed, aptly-named finish right along the edge of the face.
beta: From the col between Vesper and Sperry Peaks, an obvious ledge system cuts across the north face at roughly 5,800 ft, starting at a small notch overlooking the Vesper Glacier. The climbing is sustained low-5th-class rock with the crux exposed traverse pitch reported on pitch 5 (some parties also flag a 5.7 slab on pitch 2); belays are a mix of fixed (bolted/pin) anchors and gear anchors atop pitches 1 and 3.
